title: Cross-SDK resumable streaming + deterministic rerank parity for embeddings
creator: Maya Torres
description: Implement a cross-language SDK feature set to provide resumable streaming for embedding + rerank flows, deterministic rerank ordering across retries, and ergonomics helpers for pagination and batching. This ticket covers API surface, client-side retry semantics, cursor + checkpoint encoding, and example snippets for Python/TS/Go.
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) expose a documented streaming API that can resume after transient network failures using a compact checkpoint token
Reranking flows produce deterministic tie-breaker logic so that rerank ordering is stable across retries and partial responses
SDKs include pagination and batching helper utilities that are API-parity compatible and have unit tests for edge cases (empty pages, partial batch failures)
Examples (one per SDK) demonstrating end-to-end embeddings -> rerank with streaming, resume, and pagination exist in the repo and are referenced in docs
Automated integration test (flaky-tolerant) that simulates a mid-stream disconnect and verifies resume + final ordering is green on CI
technical_design: Checkpoint token: base64-encoded JSON string with: model, request_id, last_token_index, optional KV cache hash; small, opaque to app code
Deterministic rerank: server returns score + stable_id; client-side stable comparator uses (score desc, stable_id asc) and deterministic tie-break hash seeded from request_id
Retry semantics: idempotent resume token for non-terminal streaming states; full retry for server-side finalization errors
Pagination helpers: Cursor object that abstracts page tokens and exposes async/iterable helpers for chunking and prefetching; single canonical interface across SDKs
Batching helpers: client-side batcher supports max_tokens, max_items, and time-window flush; pluggable backpressure hooks for runtime tuning
plan: Week 1: Finalize checkpoint token format + review with API/design (design doc linked)
Week 1: Implement Python SDK streaming resume + pagination helper; add unit tests
Week 2: Port to TypeScript SDK; iterate ergonomics based on Python feedback
Week 2: Implement Go SDK primitives (synchronous iterator / channel-based resume API)
Week 3: Add integration tests that inject mid-stream disconnects; run on CI cluster
Week 3: Docs + examples for each SDK, cross-link to console/observability guide for debugging resume failures
Post-merge: Monitor error rates and latency in staging for two weeks; collect developer feedback
